item.text:
This pass refined F28’s impact by tracing how the no-command Accept state would interact with the wire codec.

In memory, the no-command acceptor records `vbal=5` with `Status=NONE` and no command ([output](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-18_00-19-47-swiftpaxos_epaxos-baseline/work/audit_accept_novalue_output.txt)). On the captured wire path, F2 drops `PrepareReply.VBallot`, so the reply arrives with `VBallot=0`. That does not remove the hazard: an empty reply at ballot 0 can tie and, if processed later, overwrite a real preaccepted reply at ballot 0 in the `>=` adoption loop. F28 therefore remains a High recovery-selection defect even with F2 present.

The audit remains at **28 findings**, **43 failing finding tests**, and **5 passing controls**; captured source is unchanged and builds cleanly. The interaction is documented in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-18_00-19-47-swiftpaxos_epaxos-baseline/work/report.md), with supporting [validation matrix](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-18_00-19-47-swiftpaxos_epaxos-baseline/work/validation_matrix.md), [remediation map](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-18_00-19-47-swiftpaxos_epaxos-baseline/work/remediation.md), and [handoff check](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-18_00-19-47-swiftpaxos_epaxos-baseline/work/handoff_check.txt).
